correctness.rationale: The mathematical argument is correct. In a perfect matching of the induced complete multipartite graph, every selected vertex in a part must match outside that part, giving \(s_i\le t\). Conversely, a complete multipartite graph on \(2t\) vertices with largest part at most \(t\) has a perfect matching; the selected set meets at least two parts and therefore dominates. The overloaded-part events in a \(2t\)-set are disjoint, giving the coefficient formula. Every valid set of size greater than two contains a cross-part edge, which itself is paired dominating, so the inclusion-minimal sets are exactly the edges. The package verifier independently confirms the criterion and coefficients through order nine.

originality.rationale: A published Resultary/SCOPE record already states the same complete-multipartite paired-domination characterization and exactly the same coefficient formula: 'Paired-domination polynomial of complete multipartite graphs' (record SCOPE-20261004-ea2bc935cbba). Its full RESULT.md was inspected. It says \(|S|=2q\) and \(s_i\le q\) for every part if and only if \(S\) is paired dominating, gives the identical double-sum coefficient formula, states all odd coefficients vanish, and gives \(d_p(G,2)=|E(G)|\) and \(\gamma_p(G)=2\). The submitted additional sentence that every inclusion-minimal paired-dominating set is an edge follows immediately from that iff criterion, because every larger valid set contains a valid cross-part two-set. Thus the entire submitted claim is covered or a routine corollary of an already published stronger result.

final_claim: For a connected complete multipartite graph \(K_{n_1,\ldots,n_r}\), a set \(S\) of size \(2t\) is paired dominating exactly when every part contributes at most \(t\) selected vertices; this yields the displayed coefficient formula. Inclusion-minimal paired-dominating sets are exactly cross-part pairs, so \(\gamma_{pr}=\Gamma_{pr}=2\) and their number is \(|E(G)|\).
limitations: Scientific rejection is for originality and value, not correctness.
